analyzed_vuln.description: Heap-buffer-overflow read occurs during deserialization of vertices when decoding attribute marker names. In SkVertices::Decode(), each encoded attribute with fHasMarkerName set calls reader.readString() and passes the returned pointer directly to SkVertices::Attribute ctor. Attribute ctor computes strlen(markerName) (line 36) without ensuring the string is NUL-terminated within the input buffer. A malformed serialized vertices blob can make readString return a pointer to bytes lacking a terminator at buffer end, so strlen reads past allocation.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: PoV flows through SkImageFilter::Deserialize -> SkPictureImageFilterImpl::CreateProc -> SkPicturePriv::MakeFromBuffer -> SkPictureData::parseBufferTag(SK_PICT_VERTICES_BUFFER_TAG) -> create_vertices_from_buffer -> SkVertices::Decode on attacker-controlled byte array from SkReadBuffer::readByteArrayAsData. Trigger requires a crafted SkVertices payload with attrCount>0 and an EncodedAttribute having fHasMarkerName=1, plus marker-name bytes that are not properly NUL-terminated before the end of the allocated data block, causing out-of-bounds read in Attribute::Attribute via strlen.
